description.value: A translational investigation examined how the rs2023239 variant of CNR1 relates to CB1 binding, alcohol cue-elicited brain activation, subjective alcohol reward, craving, and treatment outcomes.

spans.text: The present investigation encompassed multiple approaches, including receptor binding in postmortem brain tissue, functional magnetic resonance imaging, human laboratory models, and analyses of treatment outcome data.

value: The CT group demonstrated greater activation when alcohol was contrasted with inactive (ie, rest) and active (ie, litchi juice) appetitive controls in the NAcc, VMPFC, VTA, and OFC compared with the TT group.
The findings suggest that the C allele of rs2023239 is associated with greater activation of the NAcc, OFC, VTA, and VMPFC during exposure to alcohol vs either rest or control cues.

name.value: Cue-elicited brain activation correlations with alcohol use disorder and craving measures

definition.value: Pearson product moment correlations were performed between region-of-interest peak percentage signal change values and AUDIT and AUQ scores.

spans.text: The only correlations that were significant in the TT group were the correlations between the left and right OFC and the AUDIT score ( r = 0.42, P < .05 and r = 0.51, P = .01) ( Table ).

label.value: alcohol use disorder score, measured using the AUDIT

spans.text: In the CT group, the alcohol use disorder score, measured using the AUDIT, was significantly correlated with activation of the NAcc ( r = 0.83, P = .003) and the VMPFC ( r = 0.68, P = .03) using the alcohol vs active control contrast.

value: In the CT group, the alcohol use disorder score, measured using the AUDIT, was significantly correlated with activation of the NAcc and the VMPFC using the alcohol vs active control contrast.
The findings suggest that activation in response to alcohol cues is strongly associated with alcohol use disorder in individuals with the CT genotype.
